title: Contraction of a field complex onto its single cohomology
statement: Let R be a field and P an integer-indexed cochain complex of module sheaves on Spec R [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-derived-category]. For an integer j, suppose H^q(P) is zero for every integer q different from j. Then P is homotopy equivalent to the single complex on its actual homology sheaf H^j(P) in degree j. No boundedness, local freeness, rank or basis is assumed.

source.place: Proof step 4; vector-space splitting spelled out in lem-pc-finite-free-single-field-fibre proof step 2.

proof.text: The proven global-sections equivalence isEquivalence_moduleSpecΓFunctor identifies module sheaves on Spec R with R-vector spaces. Module.projective_of_isSemisimpleRing and Module.injective_of_isSemisimpleRing, together with categorical reflection along a fully faithful equivalence, prove every module sheaf projective and injective. This uses only existing proved source-library and Mathlib results.

For H=H^j(P), lift id_H across π:Z^j(P)→H using projectivity to obtain s with s≫π=id_H. Extend π across the monomorphism i:Z^j(P)→P^j using injectivity to obtain r with i≫r=π. The equations d≫r=0 and s≫i≫d=0 give a:P→single_j(H) and b:single_j(H)→P. Componentwise, b≫a=id_single: in degree j this follows from s≫i≫r=s≫π=id_H, and in every other degree the single complex term is zero.

The cycles map of a≫b in degree j is π≫s, by cancelling the cycles inclusion. Cancelling π in homology naturality shows H^j(a≫b)=id. In all other degrees the hypothesis gives a zero homology object, whose endomorphisms agree. Therefore every homology map of a≫b-id_P is zero.

Apply lem-pc-split-category-null-homotopy to a≫b-id_P and convert the resulting homotopy to zero via Homotopy.equivSubZero into a homotopy a≫b~id_P. Together with b≫a=id_single, this is the required HomotopyEquiv. The proof remains degreewise for unbounded complexes and also applies when H is zero.

proof_origin.place: Field-complex contraction in step 4, as expanded in the original node. B2 implements it by split-category null homotopies and projective/injective lifts rather than a termwise homology complex.
